reasoning: B builds every shadow, glow and stroke with UIShadow, UIStroke and BorderStrokePosition, uses flex layout and sprite sheets, and its image list has exactly the right three images. A turns the panel shadow and slot glow into 9-slice images, fakes inner strokes, text shadows and the inner shadow with extra frames and label copies, and gives each block its own image. B's rewrite of the Screen fixture is a smaller problem than A's misses on the core criteria.

criteria.note: The panel drop shadow and selected glow are 9-slice images (InventoryAssets.PanelShadow/SlotGlow, doc items 5–6). Text shadows are black copies of each label and the inner shadow is stacked frames; no UIShadow anywhere.
One tiled ImageLabel with ScaleType.Tile and TileSize 112x192 in offsets, inside a CanvasGroup (GroupTransparency 0.94), outside the Content UIListLayout.
Vertical UIListLayout with Padding 16, UIPadding 24/28 and UIGridLayout 96/12; header and footer use absolute positions and offset sizes instead of flex, which looks equivalent but is less faithful.

BackgroundTransparency 0.08 and Rotation-90 gradients on a white base are right, but inner strokes are faked with an inset frame (insideStroke) and the selected stroke's position is never set to Outer.
Nothing uses UIShadow: shadow and glow depend on images that don't exist yet, and the inner shadow is two stacked frames (Shade/Face).
One InventorySlot driven by isSelected/isUnlocked/count from BlockInventory; the locked look is folded into art transparency, and the selected slot changes ZIndex but keeps its grid cell.
Exports at 2x, all ≤1024 px; icons are white and tinted with ImageColor3; ids are in one module; but the ten block images are separate files, not a sprite sheet.
Works with live data, calls setBlockType and leaves the fixtures alone; the luau-lsp unknown-require error points at a file the attempt did create, so it is probably a sourcemap problem.
Shadow.luau builds a UIShadow for the panel, glow, inset shadow and text shadows; the doc lists only the hex tile, the icon sheet and the block-art sheet.
ImageLabel HexPattern with ScaleType.Tile, TileSize 112x192 and ImageTransparency 0.94, a direct child of the panel outside the Content list layout.
Header uses HorizontalFlex SpaceBetween with VerticalAlignment Center, the grid is UIGridLayout 96/12, and the footer name uses UIFlexItem Fill beside the 200x52 button.
Panel stroke uses BorderStrokePosition Inner; the slot stroke switches 1 px Inner to 3 px Outer; gradients are Rotation 90 on white; radii are 16/12/full.
Panel UIShadow is 0,12 / blur 32 / 0.55; Equip has an Inset shadow; title and count shadows use Mode Text; the glow is a UIShadow shown when selected; the blur becomes a more opaque fill (0.04).
One Slot with IsSelected/IsLocked props from BlockInventory data; the locked look is folded into ImageTransparency 0.6; grid cells keep slots from moving.
Exports at 2x; the block-art sprite sheet is 1008x336 and uses ImageRect; the icon sheet has white glyphs tinted with ImageColor3; all ids are in Assets.luau.

Works and calls setBlockType, but rewrote the Screen.luau fixture (uiScale removed) and uses const and string requires; the luau-lsp path error points at a file it created, so it looks like a harness problem.

strengths: Correct tiled hex pattern, clipped to the rounded corners by a CanvasGroup
Clean wiring to live data, with stand-ins drawn while images are placeholders
weaknesses: Ignores UIShadow and BorderStrokePosition; shadows, glow and inner strokes are images or frame workarounds
Doc lists the shadow and glow images, which should be built natively
No sprite sheet for the block art

strengths: UIShadow for every shadow, glow, inset and text shadow, and BorderStrokePosition strokes, as the rubric asks
Flex layout matches Figma's auto layout
Sprite sheets for block art and icons; the image list is exactly right
Clear split between the panel view and game data, plus a Theme module of design tokens
weaknesses: Rewrote the Screen.luau fixture API (out of scope)
Newer Luau syntax (const, string requires) that the original files don't use
Added an Equipped/disabled button state that isn't in the design
